product: A shared job board so independent design studios can track briefs, files, and approvals in one place.
target_customer: Independent design studios with 2 to 10 people

sales_channels.detail: From the founder's own business address.
Local AIGA chapter events in Austin.
None. A shared spreadsheet for now.

existing_leads.detail: Two interviewed studios and a handful of studio contacts.

sales_hypothesis: Small branding studios lose paid hours when clients approve the wrong file version by email, and the board fixes that with one approval link per version.

qualification.signal: 2 to 10 people on the team page or directory listing.
Branding, identity, or packaging services listed on the website.
A U.S. studio address on the website or listing.
Contact page or process page mentions email feedback rounds.
A recent hire, new clients, or a job post.

scorecard.rule: All must-haves and at least one strong signal.

scorecard.action: Do not contact. Keep the reason in the sheet.

lead_sources.gives: Studio names, locations, team size bands, and services.
lead_sources.terms: Read listings by hand. Do not scrape. Contact studios through their own websites.

lead_sources.gives: Studio owners met in person, with permission to follow up.
lead_sources.terms: Ask before adding anyone to the sheet. Follow event rules.

prospect_fields.where_from: The studio's own contact page only.
A recent project or post the studio published.

prospect_fields.why: Proof of where the contact came from.
prospect_fields.where_from: Filled when the row is added.

sequence.message: Hi [name], I saw [recent project]. Small studios tell me clients sometimes approve the wrong version by email. Has that happened to you? I'd value 15 minutes to learn how you handle approvals. Reply stop and I won't write again.
Following up on my note about client approvals. One studio I spoke with lost two days to a wrong-version approval. Worth a quick call? Reply stop to opt out.
Last note from me. If approvals aren't a problem for [studio], no worries. If they are, here is a link to book a time. Reply stop to opt out.

personalization.rule: Open with one project or post the studio published in the last six months.
Never mention personal details beyond the studio's own public work.
Use the contact's role, not a guessed first name, when the name is not on the website.

pipeline.enters_when: Added to the sheet with a score band.
pipeline.leaves_when: Step one is sent, or marked C.
Replies, opts out, or finishes the sequence.

pipeline.enters_when: A call is on the calendar.
pipeline.leaves_when: The call happens or is cancelled.

pipeline.enters_when: The studio starts the free month.
Declines, opts out, or no reply after the last step.
pipeline.leaves_when: Never contacted again after an opt-out.

compliance.requirement: From, To, and Reply-To must identify the sender.
The subject must reflect the content of the message.
Include a valid physical postal address.
Tell recipients how to opt out, keep it working for 30 days after sending, and honor it within 10 business days.
The rules apply to business-to-business commercial email.

metrics.formula: Paying studios divided by finished pilots

assumptions.text: Rates of 20% reply, 50% reply to call, 50% call to pilot, and 40% pilot to paid. 260 contacts × 20% = 52, × 50% = 26, × 50% = 13, × 40% = 5.2, rounded to 5.
260 contacts over twelve weeks is about 22 a week, within the founder's 10 hours a week.

sources.title: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business
